source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-32

procedures.title: Steering damper: remove and install
steps: Removal: remove the bolt from the damper pivot bracket at the relay rod.
Remove the nut from the damper pivot at the frame bracket and pull the damper out.
The damper is serviced only as a complete unit; replace it if damaged or badly worn.
Installation: put the piston rod end into the frame bracket and fit the retainers, bushings and nut.
Put the cylinder end pivot into the relay rod bracket and fit the through bolt.

procedures.title: Power steering hydraulic system: bleed
steps: Fill the reservoir to the correct level and leave it undisturbed at least 2 minutes.
Start the engine, run it only about 2 seconds, and top up if needed.
Repeat until the level stays steady after running the engine.
Raise the front so the wheels are off the ground.
Bring the engine to about 1500 rpm.
Turn the raised wheels left and right, just touching the wheel stops.
Lower the car and turn the wheels left and right on the ground.
Check the level and refill as needed.
If the oil is very foamy, let the car sit a few minutes with the engine off and repeat the procedure, and also:
notes: The 1968 Corvette uses linkage-type power steering: an engine-driven vane pump feeds a control valve that senses demand and supplies a power cylinder. Its steering gear is the manual-steering unit and is serviced as such, except for adjustment; the linkage is serviced like the manual linkage.
